dedupe_keys.name: who service availability and readiness assessment sara health facility survey tool and tracer indicators of service availability and readiness

description: SARA is the World Health Organization's standard survey for finding out what health facilities in a country can actually provide. Teams visit a sample or census of facilities and record a fixed set of tracer indicators: staff and beds, basic amenities such as power, water and communication, basic equipment, essential medicines, diagnostic capacity, and whether the facility is ready to deliver specific services such as family planning, maternal and child care and treatment of common diseases. Results give comparable service availability and readiness scores for a country and its regions, and many ministries have run SARA rounds. The questionnaires, reference manual and implementation guidance are free to download from WHO's data collection tools pages. Caveats: WHO's page describes the tool, not hosting a pooled data file, so country results must be found in national survey reports such as the Uganda SARA record, rounds are irregular, and facility samples vary. Coverage is global in design. Simulation uses: facility readiness and amenity data, including electricity and water, for health system capacity and resilience studies. Related records: the Uganda SARA essential medicines readiness data (data-uganda-sara-essential-medicines-readiness) is one national application.
